newsitem.title: UK: Spurs players' wage bill rises one mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Spurs players' wage bill rises one mln stg.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Tottenham Hotspur Plc said on Thursday the cost of paying its players had risen by one million stg in the six months to January 31.
Chairman Alan Sugar said the signing of four new players and the renegotiation of contracts of existing squad members had combined to push up the wage bill.

"Both of these measures have served to increase the playing department payroll by one million pounds in the first half. The full effect of this increase will be felt in the second half and future years," Sugar said in a statement.
Sugar said the higher wage bill had resulted in a 13 percent in operating costs to 10 million stg.
Operating profit before player trading rose 13 percent to 7.1 million stg while turnover rose by the same percentage to 17.1 million, thanks mainly to higher television revenue.

North London club Tottenham have been badly hit by injuries to players this season and are out of the running in all competitions. Some frustrated fans have accused the board of caring more about profits than league points.
"No-one should doubt our ambitions for this club," Sugar said in his statement.

"Football is the core activity of our business as a provider of entertainment and brand leader, and it is only when we get this right that we can fully maximise the associated business opportunities," he added.
"The playing squad has been significantly strengthened recently, and I am confident that we can look forward to the next season with high expectations of the team."
Tottenham have invested 10.8 million stg over the past six months on the purchase of Dane Allan Nielsen, Norwegian Steffen Iversen, Swiss Ramon Vega and Englishman John Scales.
